findings.claim: The depth guard in `DepthStep` changed from `>=` to `>`, an off-by-one that widens a security limit. With `MaximumObjectGraphDepth = N`, a reader already at depth N no longer throws, so N+1 nesting levels are accepted. This is unrelated to REQ-2234. It also changes behaviour when `SuppressSourceGeneration` is unset, which breaks the criterion that unflagged behaviour does not change. It also weakens the configured stack-depth protection for untrusted data (L9).

findings.claim: Before this change, two members with the same `[Key(0)]` (or the same string key) made `Dictionary.Add` throw, so the generator or analyzer failed loudly. The new `ContainsKey` guard keeps only the first member and reports no diagnostic. The generated formatter silently never serializes or deserializes the second member, which loses data without any warning. Duplicate string keys behave the same way. This applies to all users, not only those with `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`.
